controls_available: Mouse-click one of six visible ingredient jars; simplified selection loads or replaces an ingredient in the mortar.
Mouse-click one of nine curve-notch buttons; the click synchronously sets the grind step. The duration-based pestle control is unavailable in simplified mode.
Mouse-click STIR PATH; each click synchronously advances six of the 24 path samples and, at the endpoint, spends the ingredient and advances route progress only if the current gate was aligned.
Mouse-click WATER up to the four-use budget; each click synchronously moves the flask toward the origin by up to 32 px.
Mouse-click BELLOWS up to the four-use budget; each click synchronously moves the flask 22 px along its current heading, subject to map bounds.
Mouse-click SEAL to submit the current visible outcome.
No mechanic-specific keyboard handler is registered for the simplified surface; the environment's generic action declaration still includes keyboard input.
autonomous_processes: None affect the outcome in simplified mode: between agent clicks, position, heading, route progress, active ingredient, path index, budgets, and hazard contacts remain unchanged.
After a failed seal, the only Apothecary timer waits 1800 ms and removes the fresh-failure overlay/reset readout; it does not change the route, position, resources, or grading state.
The shared clock drains timers and animation frames while live, but Apothecary's animation-frame grinding loop is gated to full interaction; the simplified surface has no autonomous world update.
grouped_control_modes: Simplified jar selection or replacement (load_ingredient/replace_ingredient via jar_select)
Synchronous path progression and route commit (stir via ladle_click)

clause_i.reason: For the plausible route-choice mode covering jar and notch decisions across all generated seeds, an observation-free q(I_t) cannot choose the seed-specific ingredient/notch sequence: generation shuffles the ingredient records and independently shuffles the route grind-step schedule, then enforces unique visible gate matches. This is static visual dependence, not a real-time witness.

clause_ii.reason: For that static route-choice mode, the bounded current screenshot can show the gate, jars, notch controls, and any revealed path needed for the next choice; because the task state does not evolve during the delay, the same visible state remains the delayed-action state. This does not supply a changing process.

clause_iii.reason: No legitimate grouped mode, Delta > 0, and bounded window can witness the required strict loss. Every outcome-affecting simplified handler updates state synchronously on the click, and no task state changes autonomously between clicks. The 1800 ms post-failure callback changes only administrative UI, while any loss from the live play-time ceiling is clock-only and explicitly excluded.

common_visible_process: None. The generator creates a seed-dependent but static world; simplified browser actions synchronously mutate the model. The only delayed visual change is the post-failure overlay timeout, which is unrelated to outcome-affecting control and cannot make an action expire.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails at clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change the catalog label. There is no autonomous outcome phase in the simplified configuration to assess.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 2 is the six-ingredient, four-route, nine-notch configuration with four-use water and bellows budgets; simplified is implemented as jar selection plus discrete curve-notch buttons, and the configured observation window is 240 ms with one frame.

The generator reads the injected difficulty parameters, derives a seed-dependent static world and unique route gates, and exports geometry/mechanics/parameters as public and hidden state; its grind tick is a mechanic constant, not a running task process.
Ingredient loading, stirring, water, and bellows mutate the model inside synchronous event handlers; stirring advances a fixed six-sample stride and recovery moves are resolved immediately.

The only duration-based grinding loop is explicitly restricted to full interaction; simplified rendering creates notch buttons and wires clicks to grind_set, then wires the remaining visible controls to click handlers.
The sole Apothecary setTimeout is the 1800 ms fresh-failure UI cleanup, which only removes the failure marker and resets the readout.
The pestle animation is gated by data-grinding=true and the simplified pestle is disabled; the remaining CSS transitions/verdict styling do not alter task outcome.

The grader binds jar and grinding events to the selected interaction surface, replays route/path/recovery geometry from the submitted event transcript, and bases success on final route/effect/resource state rather than elapsed time.
Verification loads the exported result and invokes the independent Apothecary replay grader.

The solver's simplified branch uses ordinary jar and notch clicks and repeated synchronous STIR PATH clicks; its private ground-truth reads are implementation evidence, not information assumed for the classification.

The shared controller drains timers and animation frames only while the task clock is running and otherwise polls control status; it supplies clock infrastructure but no Apothecary state transition in simplified mode.
